name: Canes Venatici
introduction: is the pair of Hunting Dogs held on a leash by Boötes as they chase the Great Bear around the pole. Johannes Hevelius created the constellation in 1687 from faint stars below the Big Dipper’s handle. It is best seen on northern spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: This faint patch of sky looks away from the Milky Way and opens a window onto galaxies. The Whirlpool Galaxy, M51, was the first galaxy whose spiral arms were recognized, in drawings made by Lord Rosse in 1845. It is interacting with a smaller companion galaxy.
The globular cluster M3, with about half a million stars, is one of the finest in the northern sky.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Cor Caroli](hip:63125), “Charles’s heart”, was named in honor of King Charles I of England. It is the prototype of a class of stars with strong magnetic fields and patches of unusual chemical elements on their surfaces, which change their brightness as they rotate.

[Chara](hip:61317), only 28 light-years away, is very similar to the Sun, which has made it a favorite target in the search for habitable planets. Nearby, the carbon star Y Canum Venaticorum is so deep red that it was nicknamed La Superba.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Canes Venatici is rich in galaxies, including the Sunflower Galaxy, M63, M94, with its bright ring of star formation, and M106, whose nucleus hosts an active supermassive black hole.
